# tes-scripts.R

```{r}
devtools::load_all()

# generate trends
trends <- make_trends_dist(n = 500, d = 2, seed = 32026)
plot(trends$x1, type = "l", col = 'red',
     xlab = "t", ylab = expression(mu[t]))
lines(trends$x2, col = "blue")

# add ARMA noise
sim <- add_noise(trends,
                 h             = 30,
                 lambda_target = 4,
                 scale         = 1,
                 order         = c(2, 1),
                 s             = 100,
                 n_start       = 30,
                 seed          = 31726)

# summary of added noise processes
sim$noise

# plot observed series with true trends overlaid
plot(sim$y1, type = "l", col = 'red',
     xlab = 't', ylab = expression(X[t]))
lines(sim$y2, col = "blue")
lines(sim$x1, col = "darkgrey", lwd = 2)
lines(sim$x2, col = "darkgrey", lwd = 2)

# local moving average decoupling (method = "boot", "mc", or "analytic")
out <- lomad(sim$y1, sim$y2, q = 10, h = 50, B = 100, 
             seed = 31726, method = "boot", ncores = parallel::detectCores() - 1,
             verbose = TRUE)
out$p_values
out$observed
out$expected

# plot
plot_lomad_fit(sim$y1, sim$y2, out)

# plot smoothed trends only
plot(out$ma1, type = "l", col = "red")
lines(out$ma2, type = "l", col = "blue")
lines(out$trend_hat, type = 'l', col = 'grey')

```

```{r}

library(zoo)
library(roll)

# moving average window length
q <- 10
# window width - 
h <- 50

# correlation threshhold
x_thresh <- 0.8

# smoothed series
ma1 <- out$ma1
ma2 <- out$ma2

# estimated trend
# if you had to only estimate one - trend_hat
trend <- out$trend_hat

# smoothed noise
noise1_sm <- ma1 - trend
noise2_sm <- ma2 - trend

# oracle SNR: use the same h and s as the add_noise call so that the
# local variances here match what make_noise targeted during calibration.
# previous code used q=10 (MA window) and h=50 (variance window) which
# both differ from the add_noise parameters h=30 and s=100, causing
# lambda to appear far below lambda_target.
h_noise <- 30   # matches h in add_noise call above
s_noise <- 100  # matches s in add_noise call above

# MA-smooth true trend and true noise with add_noise's window
trend_sm_true <- roll::roll_mean(sim$x1, width = h_noise, min_obs = h_noise)
noise1_true   <- sim$y1 - sim$x1
noise2_true   <- sim$y2 - sim$x2
e1_sm         <- roll::roll_mean(noise1_true, width = h_noise, min_obs = h_noise)
e2_sm         <- roll::roll_mean(noise2_true, width = h_noise, min_obs = h_noise)

# local variances using add_noise's variance window
lv_signal <- roll::roll_var(trend_sm_true, width = s_noise, center = TRUE, min_obs = s_noise)
lv_noise1 <- roll::roll_var(e1_sm,         width = s_noise, center = TRUE, min_obs = s_noise)
lv_noise2 <- roll::roll_var(e2_sm,         width = s_noise, center = TRUE, min_obs = s_noise)

lambda1 <- lv_signal / lv_noise1
lambda2 <- lv_signal / lv_noise2

#rho 
rho_t <- sqrt((lambda1 * lambda2) /
              ((1 + lambda1) * (1 + lambda2)))

# starting with neff = h = 50 - will change later
n_eff <- h
z_t <- sqrt(n_eff) * (x_thresh - rho_t)
p_t <- pnorm(z_t)

plot(rho_t, type = "l")
plot(lv_signal, type = "l")

#histogram of lambdas 
hist(lambda1, 
     main = "Lambda 1",
     breaks = 50) 

hist(lambda2, main = "lambda 2", 
     breaks = 50)
```


## Approach 2 

```{r}
# theoretical smoothed trend over same q window length
trend_sm_true <- stats::filter(sim$x1, rep(1/q, q), sides = 1)

# theoretical vairance of smoothed trend
tau2_t_theory <- zoo::rollapply(
  trend_sm_true,
  width = h,
  FUN = var,
  align = "right",
  fill = NA
)

#arma parameters from noise process
ar1 <- sim$noise$series1$ar
ma1_coef <- sim$noise$series1$ma
innov_var1 <- sim$noise$series1$sigma^2

ar2 <- sim$noise$series2$ar
ma2_coef <- sim$noise$series2$ma
innov_var2 <- sim$noise$series2$sigma^2

# noise autocovariance computation
lag_max <- 200
# gammaZ = vector of noise autocovariances
gammaZ1 <- stats::ARMAacf(ar = ar1, ma = ma1_coef, lag.max = lag_max) * innov_var1
gammaZ2 <- stats::ARMAacf(ar = ar2, ma = ma2_coef, lag.max = lag_max) * innov_var2

# smoothing noise autocovariance
# smoothed-noise covariance as the double sum over the autocovariance.
gamma_eta_at_lag <- function(gammaZ, lag, q) {
  total <- 0
  for (i in 0:(q - 1)) {
    for (j in 0:(q - 1)) {
      idx <- abs(lag + i - j) + 1
      total <- total + gammaZ[idx]
    }
  }
  total / q^2
}

gammaEta1 <- sapply(0:lag_max, function(L) gamma_eta_at_lag(gammaZ1, L, q))
gammaEta2 <- sapply(0:lag_max, function(L) gamma_eta_at_lag(gammaZ2, L, q))

# theoretical smoothed noise covariances
sigma1_sq_theory <- gammaEta1[1]
sigma2_sq_theory <- gammaEta2[1]

# compute theoritical lambda values
lambda1_theory <- tau2_t_theory / sigma1_sq_theory
lambda2_theory <- tau2_t_theory / sigma2_sq_theory

# correlation 
rho_t_theory <- sqrt((lambda1_theory * lambda2_theory) /
                     ((1 + lambda1_theory) * (1 + lambda2_theory)))

# full probability calculation 
n_eff_theory <- h
z_t_theory <- sqrt(n_eff_theory) * (x_thresh - rho_t_theory)
p_t_theory <- pnorm(z_t_theory)


# lambdas check 
summary(lambda1_theory)
summary(lambda2_theory)

hist(lambda1_theory, 
     main = "Lambda 1 Theory",
     breaks = 50) 

# shows higher lambda 2 values unlike data based approach
hist(lambda2_theory, main = "lambda 2 Theory", 
     breaks = 50)

```


# Approach 1 vs 2 Rho

```{r}
# higher correlations shown with theoretical values approach 2
plot(rho_t_theory, type = "l")
plot(rho_t, type = "l")
```
